quote: But everyone in our family says don’t tell him. Avoid it at all costs. Even our kids know that. Unfortunately we live close by and if my kids so much as go on a bike ride they see him.
cx: Early first trimester with a fourth baby; her father-in-law reacts badly to every pregnancy announcement.

quote: while I’m still early in the first trimester I’m so sick already. I’ve skipped two family functions because of it. It’s getting harder to hide.
cx: Same post: hiding the pregnancy from a neighbour-relative.

quote: Oh a myriad of things complete with a string of F-bombs and statements about how stupid we are.
cx: What her father-in-law said at past announcements.

quote: We're moving to the new university in 2 weeks. I think we'll like it.  It's in a small city in the upper Midwest and it's within a day drive of both my parents and her parents, but we don't know anyone there yet.
cx: A new father starting a paid PhD post weeks after the birth; they have lived with his parents all summer.

quote: I want to be a provider and caretaker for my family, but I also need to be able to focus on work so that I can provide for them. The best advice I've heard so far is to be at home when you're at home and at work when you're at work
cx: Same father on going back to work.

quote: They were joking about how many paper towels I use, how I clean the counters twice, and then his mom said “I don’t know why your wife that is home all day doesn’t stain the cabinets.”
cx: 18 weeks, first baby, not working; cooking dinner for her husband and mother-in-law.

quote: I told him I got very tired from grocery shopping (the heat index was 110° where I live) […] He also said he can’t help but roll his eyes when I say I’m tired from just going to the store when I didn’t do anything else in the day
cx: What her husband told her when he admitted feeling resentful.

quote: I also told him I was disappointed that he was doing zero research into what I was going through and that he had unrealistic expectations. He did do some research and he did talk to some of his female relatives and started helping out more around the house and being more empathetic.
cx: What changed her husband in the first trimester.

quote:
My overnight rate is $45/hour. […] The challenge is that she charged $30/hour, and my rate is $45/hour.

The family asked if I had any flexibility.
cx: An overnight postpartum doula, the only one in her area, quoting a family due in December.

quote: I completely understand where they’re coming from, especially because they’re also paying someone to help with daytime household tasks now, which they weren’t doing with their last baby. I offered to reduce my overnight rate to $40/hour because they’re looking at booking a large package, but they’re still not comfortable with the total cost.
cx: Why a returning family is pushing on her price.

quote: She insists that combination feeding is harmful. I’m trying to my best to look into it (my background is in academia) but only see anecdotal evidence for either case. […] My wife can’t tell me why combination feeding is bad. She’s simply heard it from her friends.
cx: A first-time father at six weeks, feeds lasting hours and no one sleeping.
